results.claim_label: Maguire v. Sierra Conservation Center (ADJ12317646) -- a real boundary case

transitions.from_report: PQME Dr. Amster, report (Jan 27, 2021) -- Exhibit 6, p.22
transitions.to_report: PQME Dr. Amster, report (Nov 16, 2021) -- Exhibit 5, p.19

diagnosis_text_changed_informational.from: Right shoulder (2014), left shoulder (2018), lumbar spine, bilateral shoulders, eyes, hernia, cardiovascular system (cumulative injury)
diagnosis_text_changed_informational.to: Same body parts as prior report, PLUS newly found bilateral hip injury (cumulative trauma)

results.real_outcome: Petition for reconsideration DENIED. Included deliberately as a real NEGATIVE/boundary result: PQME Dr. Amster's real reports add bilateral hips as a newly-found injured body part between Jan and Nov 2021 -- a real diagnosis-scope expansion with NO accompanying severity signal (no surgery, prognosis, or work-capacity change at these citations). The engine correctly does NOT flag this as material, which is honest and correct given its rules, but is a real, disclosed gap: scope expansion alone isn't caught unless paired with an objective severity change.

results.real_outcome: Petition for reconsideration GRANTED on the permanent-disability percentage. Included as a real NEGATIVE/boundary result found while checking whether LLM-based extraction could scale this further: QME Dr. Feingold's real apportionment opinion shifted from 80%-non-industrial/20%-industrial to a 50/50 split after reviewing an MRI -- a real, meaningful escalation in compensable share, but one this engine's schema has no field for (it models diagnosis/treatment/prognosis/recovery/impairment/work-capacity, not apportionment percentage). Correctly reported as no material change by the engine's existing rules; a real, disclosed gap in what the schema covers, not a bug.
